findings.title: Dayjs objects compared with === instead of .isSame()
findings.body: The expression `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes") === dayjs(date.end).add(utcOffset, "minutes")` compares two distinct Dayjs object references with strict equality. This will always evaluate to `false`, meaning the check for a zero-length date override (which typically represents a day-off/unavailable day) will never trigger. Should use `.isSame()` instead.

findings.title: Working hours end-time check uses slotStartTime instead of slotEndTime
findings.body: The variable `end` is computed as `slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute()`, which is identical to `start`. It should use `slotEndTime` to verify the entire slot (start + eventLength) fits within working hours. As written, a slot that starts within working hours but extends past the end of the working window will be incorrectly considered available.

findings.title: Working hours availability check logic is inverted for multiple time blocks
findings.body: The `workingHours.find(...)` returns the first working-hour block where the slot does NOT fit, and then marks the slot as unavailable. If a user has multiple working-hour blocks on the same day (e.g., 9–12 and 14–17), a slot at 14:00 will fail the check against the 9–12 block and be incorrectly rejected, even though it fits within 14–17. The logic should only reject the slot if it doesn't fit within ANY working-hour block for that day.

findings.title: Multiple date overrides on the same day can incorrectly reject available slots
findings.body: The `dateOverrides.find(...)` callback returns `true` (marking the slot as outside the override) for the first override on the matching day where the slot doesn't fit. If there are multiple overrides on the same day and the slot falls within one of them but not another, `find` may return the non-matching override and the slot is rejected. The logic should check whether the slot is within ANY override on that day before rejecting it.

findings.title: override.timeZone may be undefined, causing dayjs.tz() to behave unpredictably
findings.body: The `TimeRange` type defines `timeZone` as optional (`timeZone?: string`). If a date override lacks a `timeZone` value, `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(undefined)` will not produce a meaningful offset, potentially causing incorrect slot calculations or runtime errors. A fallback (e.g., to `organizerTimeZone`) should be provided.

findings.title: Using .toString() on Date before passing to dayjs is fragile
findings.body: `dayjs(override.start.toString())` converts the Date to a locale-dependent string representation (e.g., 'Thu Jan 01 1970 14:00:00 GMT+0000') and then re-parses it. This is unnecessary since `dayjs(override.start)` accepts Date objects directly, and the string format may not parse reliably across environments or locales.

findings.title: No test for round-robin fixed host date override scenario
findings.body: The PR description states it fixes date overrides of fixed hosts being taken into account for round-robin events, but no test is added that verifies this behavior (e.g., a round-robin event with a fixed host who has a date override, ensuring only the fixed host's override slots are shown). Only the timezone adjustment for personal events is tested.
